elements.element: Customer has no obligation to pay liquidated damages.
elements.evidence: The Company must pay a predetermined Termination Payment upon a qualifying convenience termination, calculated by reference to the preceding three months’ fees.

elements.element: Customer has no obligation to pay penalties.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause does not impose a separate penalty; it provides only for the specified Termination Payment.

elements.element: Any liquidated amount payable by Customer is triggered only by Customer’s early termination.
elements.evidence: The Termination Payment applies only if the Company terminates for convenience under Section 4.1 and expressly excludes termination for HDI’s breach, failure to perform, or under Section 1.6.

elements.element: The early-termination fee does not exceed three months’ fees.
elements.evidence: The Termination Payment equals the aggregate fees payable under Section 3.1 for the three calendar months preceding the Termination Date, so it cannot exceed that three-month measure.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer because of the termination.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the Termination Payment is the “sole and exclusive amount payable by the Company by reason of such termination.”

result.reason: The redline retains a liquidated termination payment, so it fails the preferred position but satisfies each fallback requirement. It is not minimal and may affect unrelated termination economics because “sole and exclusive amount payable” is broader than “sole liquidated amount” and could be read to displace other amounts payable upon termination. The retained dangling sentence beginning “Payment is determined” is also grammatically defective and no longer fits the revised nonnegative fee formula.
